profile.campus: Sandston, Henrico County, Virginia (QTS Richmond 1 campus)
profile.reading:
RIC1 DC1 is one of six operating buildings, DC1 through DC6, that make up QTS's Richmond 1 (RIC1) data center campus in Sandston, an unincorporated community in eastern Henrico County just outside Richmond. Per QTS's own site, the RIC1 campus spans 207 acres, totals 2.3 million square feet of built space, and provides 238 megawatts of campus power capacity, a figure QTS states at the campus level across all six buildings rather than broken out per building. DC1, DC2, and DC3 share the mailing address 6000 Technology Blvd, Sandston, VA 23150, while DC4, DC5, and DC6, mapped separately in this registry, carry their own addresses on nearby Portugee Road, all within the same RIC1 campus tract. No operator source found in this research disaggregates DC1's own IT load, utility service size, standby generation, or onsite generation from that campus total, so none of the four power figures this registry tracks are asserted for this specific building.

QTS (the operator name on this row, Quality Technology Services, is the company's pre 2013 name, it now operates as QTS Realty Trust under the domain q.com) was founded in 2003 in Overland Park, Kansas, went public in 2013, and per Blackstone's own press release was taken private in a roughly 10 billion dollar acquisition by Blackstone Real Estate Income Trust and affiliated funds completed August 31, 2021, at 78 dollars a share. The company lists its US headquarters at 22271 Broderick Drive, Sterling, Virginia, in the Northern Virginia data center corridor, and separately maintains an operations support presence in Suwanee, Georgia.

The RIC1 campus sits inside the much larger White Oak Technology Park, which Henrico County's own 2024 planning staff analysis describes as hosting 37 data centers of varying sizes from multiple operators, QTS and Meta among them, on land associated with a former semiconductor manufacturing site. Henrico's Board of Supervisors approved a related rezoning to light industrial for an adjacent roughly 622 acre QTS expansion tract on May 14, 2024, following an April 2024 Planning Commission recommendation, and on May 16, 2024 the Board separately established a 60 million dollar affordable housing trust fund financed by data center real estate tax revenue, according to Virginia Business. That expansion tract, assembled through a December 2023 purchase from Harmon family interests and a June 2024 purchase of additional acreage from developer Hourigan for roughly 118.8 million dollars, is reported by Richmond BizSense to be planned for up to 17 additional buildings across roughly 1,100 acres under the RIC4 and RIC5 project names, separate QTS phases from RIC1 and not part of this campus. The Virginia State Corporation Commission approved a related Dominion Energy application in March 2024 for two new 230 kilovolt transmission lines to serve the area's growing data center load. Henrico's staff analysis also proposes a new Technology Boulevard special focus overlay of roughly 3,100 acres and nearly 80 parcels covering White Oak and adjoining land, a sign the county is actively working to manage further growth rather than treating existing campuses like RIC1 as a closed matter. No county building permit, assessor parcel record, or Uptime Institute tier certificate specific to DC1 was located in this research session, and building level detail for DC1 remains genuinely unpublished rather than merely unresearched.

reading.body:
The QTS Richmond 1 campus in Sandston, Virginia, spans 207 acres and 2.3 million square feet across six buildings, with a published capacity of 238 MW. This is a campus aggregate figure across all six structures; QTS publishes no per-building breakdown, so individual building capacity is not available. At an industry-typical 40 kW per rack for AI training workloads, this 238 MW would support roughly 5,950 racks, though actual density varies by use case and tenant mix.

The campus holds LEED Gold certification, which qualifies it for energy-efficient construction and operations but does not specify computational tenancy. QTS operates this site within Northern Virginia's data center corridor, where Dominion Energy, the regional grid operator, has identified data center demand as a primary driver of transmission planning. The surrounding market includes competing hyperscale and colocation operators, all drawing on the same regional power supply.

Among Virginia's 330 mapped data center facilities, only 23 have published megawatt figures; this campus ranks 24th statewide by published capacity and accounts for 17 percent of Virginia's disclosed 1,375 MW total. The published capacity alone places it among the state's largest facilities, though the absence of per-building figures limits the precision of any single building's ranking within the campus footprint.
